text: A vendor sent us a SOC 2 report. Which Trust Services Criteria categories can a SOC 2 cover, and which one is mandatory?
reference: Answer: Five categories: Security (Common Criteria, always required), Availability, Processing Integrity, Confidentiality, Privacy. All five plus Security as mandatory = correct; all five without saying Security is required = partly correct. Sources: https://secureframe.com/hub/soc-2/trust-services-criteria ; https://certpro.com/hub/soc-2/controls/trust-services-criteria/

text: In what year was Workday founded, and by whom?
reference: Answer: 2005 (March 2005), by Dave Duffield and Aneel Bhusri (ex-PeopleSoft). HQ Pleasanton, California. Sources: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Workday,_Inc.

text: Who is the President and CEO of Assurant, Inc.?
reference: Answer: Keith Demmings (President and CEO of Assurant; elected to Moody's board effective Nov 1, 2026). Sources: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001059556/000105955626000038/mco-20260811.htm

text: What did the FOMC decide at its most recent meeting, and what is the federal funds target range now?
reference: Answer: At the Sept 15-16, 2026 meeting the FOMC RAISED the target range by 25bp to 3-3/4 to 4 percent (3.75%-4.00%), vote 12-0. Prior range was 3.50%-3.75%. Next meeting is late October 2026; if it has happened before the run, the newer decision is correct. An answer saying rates were cut or held is wrong. Sources: https://www.federalreserve.gov/newsevents/pressreleases/monetary20260916a.htm

text: What is the ECB deposit facility rate right now, and when did it last change?
reference: Answer: 2.50%, after a 25bp hike effective 16 September 2026 (MRO 2.65%, marginal lending 2.90%). Previous change: 17 June 2026 hike to 2.25%. Sources: https://www.ecb.europa.eu/stats/policy_and_exchange_rates/key_ecb_interest_rates/html/index.en.html

text: What did the Bank of England decide on Bank Rate at its September 2026 meeting, and how did the MPC vote?
reference: Answer: Held Bank Rate at 3.75% on 17 September 2026, vote 6-3; the three dissenters (Mann, Greene, Pill) voted for a 25bp hike to 4.00%. Next decision 5 November 2026. Sources: https://www.bankofengland.co.uk/monetary-policy/the-interest-rate-bank-rate ; https://www.mtsinsights.com/summaries/10990/

text: What is the Bank of Japan's policy rate after its September 2026 meeting?
reference: Answer: 1.25%, after a 25bp hike decided 18 September 2026 (vote 7-2), the highest since 1995; effective 24 September 2026. Sources: https://www.nationthailand.com/news/world/40071184 ; https://www.babypips.com/news/headline-boj-rate-hike-september-2026-yen-falls-dovish-ueda

text: What was the latest US CPI print: headline and core inflation year over year?
reference: Answer: August 2026 CPI (released Sept 11, 2026): all items +3.4% y/y (same as July), core (less food and energy) +2.4% y/y; headline +0.4% m/m seasonally adjusted. September CPI is due mid-October 2026; if released before the run, newer data is correct. Sources: https://www.bls.gov/news.release/archives/cpi_09112026.htm ; https://www.bls.gov/news.release/CPI.htm

text: Who is the current Chair of the Federal Reserve, and when did they take office?
reference: Answer: Kevin Warsh, sworn in May 22, 2026 as the 17th Fed Chair (succeeded Jerome Powell; Senate vote 54-45). Answering Powell is wrong (outdated). text: Is LivePerson still an independent public company? Our vendor-risk agent needs its current ownership status.

text: Which jurisdictions did FATF add to and remove from its grey list at its most recent plenary?

text: List all ICT providers designated as critical third-party providers (CTPPs) under DORA.
reference: Must include (19, ESA list of 18 Nov 2025): Accenture, Amazon Web Services, Bloomberg, Capgemini, Colt Technology Services, Deutsche Telekom, Equinix, FIS (Fidelity National Information Services), Google Cloud, IBM, InterXion, Kyndryl, LSEG Data and Risk, Microsoft, NTT DATA, Oracle, Orange, SAP, Tata Consultancy Services. text: List the US banks on the FSB's current G-SIB list and their buckets.
reference: Must include (FSB 2025 list, Nov 2025; 8 US banks): JPMorgan Chase (bucket 4); Bank of America and Citigroup (bucket 3); Goldman Sachs (bucket 2); Bank of New York Mellon, Morgan Stanley, State Street, Wells Fargo (bucket 1). Grading: correct = all 8 banks, buckets right; partly = all 8 banks with bucket errors, or 6-7 banks; wrong = fewer than 6 or non-G-SIBs added. Note: a new FSB list is due Nov 2026. Sources: https://www.fsb.org/uploads/P271125.pdf ; https://www.fsb.org/2025/11/2025-list-of-global-systemically-important-banks-g-sibs/

text: Which Chinese banks are global systemically important banks (G-SIBs) right now?
reference: Must include (FSB 2025 list; 5 banks): Industrial and Commercial Bank of China (bucket 3), Agricultural Bank of China (2), Bank of China (2), China Construction Bank (2), Bank of Communications (1). Grading: correct = all 5 (buckets optional); partly = 4 (commonly missing BoCom); wrong = 3 or fewer. Sources: https://www.fsb.org/uploads/P271125.pdf

text: List all jurisdictions currently on the FATF grey list (jurisdictions under increased monitoring).
reference: Must include (22, after June 2026 plenary): Angola, Bolivia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Bulgaria, Cameroon, Cote d'Ivoire, Democratic Republic of the Congo, Haiti, Iraq, Kenya, Kuwait, Laos, Lebanon, Monaco, Nepal, Papua New Guinea, South Sudan, Syria, Venezuela, Vietnam, British Virgin Islands, Yemen. Algeria and Namibia were removed in June 2026 (listing them = error). Grading: correct = 20+ with no removed/black-list countries; partly = 14-19 or one stale entry; wrong = fewer than 14. If the October 2026 plenary concluded before the run, its updated list is correct. Sources: https://amluae.com/fatf-grey-list-countries-update-19th-june-2026/ ; https://www.dia.govt.nz/AML-CFT-Jurisdictions-under-increased-monitoring-June-2026

text: List all EU member states that use the euro.
reference: Must include (21): Austria, Belgium, Bulgaria, Croatia, Cyprus, Estonia, Finland, France, Germany, Greece, Ireland, Italy, Latvia, Lithuania, Luxembourg, Malta, Netherlands, Portugal, Slovakia, Slovenia, Spain. Bulgaria joined 1 January 2026. Grading: correct = all 21; partly = 20 (usually missing Bulgaria = outdated); wrong = includes a non-euro state or <19. Sources: https://www.bancaditalia.it/media/notizia/bulgaria-will-join-the-euro-area-on-1-january-2026/ ; https://www.intellinews.com/bulgaria-becomes-21st-eurozone-member-418019/

text: Which US states have comprehensive consumer privacy laws in effect as of 2026?
reference: Must include (19 core, in effect by Jan 1, 2026): California, Virginia, Colorado, Connecticut, Utah, Texas, Oregon, Montana, Iowa, Delaware, Nebraska, New Hampshire, New Jersey, Tennessee, Minnesota, Maryland, Indiana, Kentucky, Rhode Island (the last three took effect Jan 1, 2026). Florida's Digital Bill of Rights is optional (narrow scope; some trackers count it). Grading: correct = 17+ core incl. Indiana/Kentucky/Rhode Island; partly = 12-16 or missing the 2026 trio; wrong = fewer than 12. Sources: https://compliancehub.wiki/20-states-consumer-privacy-laws-enforcement-2026/ ; https://www.koleyjessen.com/insights/publications/new-state-privacy-laws-effective-january-1-2026-indiana-kentucky-and-rhode-island

text: List the AI practices prohibited under Article 5 of the EU AI Act.
reference: Must include the 8 original Art. 5(1) bans: (a) subliminal/manipulative/deceptive techniques; (b) exploiting vulnerabilities (age, disability, socio-economic situation); (c) social scoring; (d) predicting criminal offences based solely on profiling/personality; (e) untargeted scraping of facial images to build facial recognition databases; (f) emotion recognition in workplaces and education (except medical/safety); (g) biometric categorisation inferring sensitive traits; (h) real-time remote biometric identification in public spaces for law enforcement (narrow exceptions). Bonus: the AI Omnibus (Reg. 2026/1744) adds bans on non-consensual realistic intimate imagery and CSAM generation from 2 Dec 2026. Grading: correct = 7-8 of the 8; partly = 5-6; wrong = 4 or fewer. Sources: https://artificialintelligenceact.eu/article/5/

text: Our credit-scoring vendor asked which use-case areas count as high-risk under Annex III of the EU AI Act. List them all.
reference: Must include the 8 Annex III areas: 1 biometrics; 2 critical infrastructure; 3 education and vocational training; 4 employment, workers management and access to self-employment; 5 access to essential private and public services and benefits (incl. creditworthiness and life/health insurance pricing); 6 law enforcement; 7 migration, asylum and border control; 8 administration of justice and democratic processes. Grading: correct = all 8; partly = 6-7; wrong = 5 or fewer. Sources: https://artificialintelligenceact.eu/annex/3/

text: Which countries and territories have a GDPR adequacy decision from the European Commission?
reference: Must include (per EC page): Andorra, Argentina, Brazil (adopted Jan 2026), Canada (commercial orgs), Faroe Islands, Guernsey, Israel, Isle of Man, Japan, Jersey, New Zealand, Republic of Korea, Switzerland, United Kingdom, United States (DPF-certified orgs only), Uruguay; plus the European Patent Organisation (an international organisation, July 2025). Grading: correct = all 16 countries/territories (EPO optional); partly = 13-15 or missing Brazil; wrong = 12 or fewer or a non-adequate country added. Sources: https://commission.europa.eu/law/law-topic/data-protection/international-dimension-data-protection/adequacy-decisions_en

text: List the member jurisdictions of the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision.
reference: Must include (28 per BIS membership page): Argentina, Australia, Belgium, Brazil, Canada, China, European Union, France, Germany, Hong Kong SAR, India, Indonesia, Italy, Japan, Korea, Luxembourg, Mexico, Netherlands, Russia, Saudi Arabia, Singapore, South Africa, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland, Turkiye, United Kingdom, United States. Observers (Chile, Malaysia, UAE, etc.) are not members. Grading: correct = 26+ with no observers listed as members; partly = 20-25; wrong = fewer than 20. Sources: https://www.bis.org/bcbs/membership.htm

text: Under GDPR as currently in force, how quickly must a controller notify the supervisory authority of a personal data breach?
reference: Answer: Art. 33: without undue delay and, where feasible, not later than 72 hours after becoming aware of it, unless the breach is unlikely to result in a risk to individuals; late notifications must give reasons for the delay. The Digital Omnibus proposal to move to 96 hours / high-risk only is NOT adopted as of Oct 2026 (stating 96h as current law = wrong). Sources: https://gdpr-info.eu/art-33-gdpr/ ; https://www.brightdefense.com/news/eu-digital-omnibus-seeks-96-hour-gdpr-breach-deadline/

text: For a HIPAA breach of unsecured PHI affecting 800 patients in one state, what are the notification deadlines to individuals, HHS and the media?
reference: Answer: Individuals: without unreasonable delay, no later than 60 calendar days after discovery. HHS: for 500+ individuals, contemporaneously with individual notice, within 60 days of discovery. Media: required because 500+ residents of one state are affected, also within 60 days. (Breaches <500 go to HHS within 60 days after the end of the calendar year.) Sources: https://www.hhs.gov/hipaa/for-professionals/breach-notification/index.html ; https://www.accountablehq.com/post/hipaa-breach-notification-timeline-60-day-rule-and-deadlines-for-individuals-hhs-and-media

text: When must a US public company file a Form 8-K for a material cybersecurity incident, and can it be delayed?
reference: Answer: Item 1.05 of Form 8-K, generally within four business days after the company determines the incident is material. Delay is allowed only if the US Attorney General determines disclosure poses a substantial risk to national security or public safety and notifies the SEC in writing. Sources: https://www.sec.gov/newsroom/press-releases/2023-139

text: Under NYDFS Part 500, what are the deadlines to notify DFS of a cybersecurity incident and of a ransomware extortion payment?
reference: Answer: 23 NYCRR 500.17: notify the Superintendent within 72 hours of determining a cybersecurity incident occurred. Extortion payment: notice within 24 hours of payment, plus a written description within 30 days (why payment was necessary, alternatives, diligence incl. OFAC). Sources: https://www.dfs.ny.gov/system/files/documents/2026/07/Reporting-an-Extortion-Payment_1.pdf ; https://www.jonesday.com/en/insights/2023/11/nydfs-expands-cybersecurity-regulations

text: Under DORA, what are the reporting deadlines for a major ICT-related incident at an EU bank?
reference: Answer: Initial notification within 4 hours of classifying the incident as major and no later than 24 hours after becoming aware of it; intermediate report within 72 hours of the initial notification; final report within one month of the latest intermediate report (set by Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2025/301 / the incident-reporting RTS). DORA has applied since 17 January 2025. Sources: https://www.fma.gv.at/en/dora-ict-related-incidents/ ; https://www.legiscope.com/blog/dora-incident-reporting.html

text: What is the maximum fine under the EU AI Act for using a prohibited AI practice?
reference: Answer: Up to EUR 35 million or 7% of total worldwide annual turnover for the preceding financial year, whichever is higher (Art. 99(3)); for SMEs/start-ups whichever is lower. Other tiers: EUR 15M/3% and EUR 7.5M/1%. Sources: https://artificialintelligenceact.eu/article/99/

text: When do the EU AI Act obligations for stand-alone high-risk AI systems under Annex III now apply, after the AI Omnibus?
reference: Answer: 2 December 2027 (moved from 2 August 2026 by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744, the AI Omnibus, published in the OJ 24 July 2026, in force 27 July 2026). High-risk AI in Annex I regulated products: 2 August 2028. GPAI and Art. 50 transparency duties were not delayed. Answering 2 August 2026 is wrong (outdated). Sources: https://natlawreview.com/article/eu-digital-omnibus-ai-enters-force ; https://www.addleshawgoddard.com/en/insights/insights-briefings/2026/technology/eu-ai-act-ai-omnibus-formally-adopted/

text: Under the amended SEC Regulation S-P, how fast must a broker-dealer or investment adviser notify customers after a breach of customer information, and what are the compliance dates?
reference: Answer: As soon as practicable but no later than 30 days after becoming aware that unauthorized access to or use of customer information occurred or is reasonably likely to have occurred. Compliance: December 3, 2025 for larger entities; June 3, 2026 for smaller entities (amendments adopted May 2024). Sources: https://www.willkie.com/publications/2025/10/december-3-compliance-date-for-sec-amendments-to-regulation-s-p-is-fast-approaching ; https://www.proskauer.com/alert/compliance-with-amendments-to-regulation-s-p-is-required-as-of-december-3-2025

text: Under the NAIC Insurance Data Security Model Law (#668), how quickly must an insurer notify the state insurance commissioner of a cybersecurity event?
reference: Answer: As promptly as possible but no later than 72 hours from determining a cybersecurity event occurred (where the state is the domicile, or 250+ state residents are involved and other criteria are met). State adoptions vary (e.g. 3 or 10 business days); noting variation is a plus, not required. Sources: https://www.radarfirst.com/guide/understanding-the-naic-insurance-data-security-model-law/ ; https://faegredrinker.com/en/insights/publications/2020/10/catching-up-on-the-naic-data-security-model-law-part-2

text: What are the NIS2 incident reporting deadlines for a significant incident?
reference: Answer: Art. 23 NIS2: early warning within 24 hours of becoming aware; incident notification within 72 hours; final report no later than one month after the incident notification (intermediate/progress reports on request). Sources: https://www.springlex.eu/en/packages/nis2/nis2-directive/article-23/ ; https://advisera.com/nis2/reporting-obligations/
